svg.title: Anatomy of a springl, and spring level sets vs. doubleweave
svg.text: attraction to the nearest neighbor vertex
A springl is a short line segment: a
particle with two arms ending in
vertexes, and a normal. Particles are
advected by the flow; the arms relax
length and turning it toward its
one constellation; the iso-contour makes the surface watertight
contour vertex on a grid edge
Springls track the interface; the level set is evolved toward
them, and its iso-contour closes the gaps between them. Springls
far from the contour are removed; uncovered edges are filled.
two staggered constellations that cover each other's gaps
dual springl covers the primal gap
Primal (red / gray) and dual (blue / orange) springls are offset
by half an edge and overlap, so their union is watertight. Each
constellation is filled and contracted against its own level set.
